record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; the paper and code were not read.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports steering and direction-recovery results bearing on refusal, but it does not report the original full-layer, all-position ablation. It tests the topic with different directions and measures.
record.gate_note: The README reports refusal-direction steering outcomes, so the repo meets the result gate. Probe-accuracy and prompt-baseline figures concern correctness prediction, not refusal-direction effects; listed scripts without reported outcomes are not results.
record.test_reason: The study's 'refusal' is abstention on factual questions it cannot answer ('As…' openings), contrasted with confabulation. It is not refusal of harmful instructions. Its direction is a refusal-vs-wrong-answer probe, SAE feature or optimized vector, not harmful-minus-harmless. The construct is related but different, so the findings go under fits_no_version, not V1 or V4. A difference-in-means script is listed, but the README reports no result from it.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct, but the refusal is abstention on unanswerable factual questions, set against confabulation, not harmful-request refusal. Directions along it steer the first-token refusal opening ('gates the opening, not the knowledge'). No SAE feature marks confabulation itself. The main thrust is that probes must beat prompt-text baselines.
record.recipe_differences: The README describes difference-in-means recovery alongside probe, SAE-feature, and optimized directions, with steering results rather than the original all-layer, all-position ablation and addition protocol. This is a research repo/preprint, not a stated replication.
record.method_sensitivity: The README reports that the direction push is at or below the state's own norm and that SAE feature 2191 uses roughly half the probe's dose; it does not give per-condition intervention rates.

fits_no_version.finding: In small instruction-tuned models, adding an abstention-vs-confabulation direction at or below state norm flips most wrong answers to refusal openings. Three such directions sit 50–81° apart and all steer. Only about 1/3 of openings complete as judged refusals, the same rate as text-prefix forcing.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Epistemic abstention (declining unanswerable factual questions) has linear directions that control the refusal opening token but not the completed refusal. Several non-collinear directions do this.

fits_no_version.finding: Pushing opposite to the abstention direction turns refusals mostly into confabulations and leaves originally correct answers intact.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Suppressing the abstention direction induces confabulation without harming known answers.

record.problems: The intervention outcomes are mostly qualitative in the README, with no stated sample sizes or uncertainty for the refusal-steering results. The model attribution for some aggregate steering findings is not stated. The reported preservation check is limited to originally correct answers, not general capability.
record.rows_left_out: No further README-reported outcomes on refusal-direction interventions were omitted. Listed scripts and result files were not treated as results; correctness-probe transfer and h_adds figures concern correctness prediction, not refusal-direction transfer.

missing.what: Difference-in-means recovery of the abstention direction compared with the probe direction (cosine or steering effect); no result is stated in the README.
Norm-matched random-direction and shuffled-probe control results for steering.
Intervention results for Gemma 2 2B (including sub-norm sweep) and Llama 3.2 3B.

record.verdict_notes: Only the README and file list were available; the paper was not read. The reader linked rows to V1/V4 because they say 'refusal direction', but the behaviour and direction differ from the claim's harmful-instruction refusal. If the claim's scope were widened to include abstention refusal, this study would bear on V4 (several non-collinear directions steer) and on V1's 'adding induces refusal' (only the opening, about 1/3 complete). Model attribution for r2 and r4–r7 is likely Qwen3-1.7B, based on file names.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report removing the direction at every layer and position, testing harmful requests, or measuring whether general capabilities are largely retained.
Does not establish an affine or cone model of refusal geometry.
